Association Football Club'' | ground = [[Oriel Park]] | coordinates = {{coord|54|00|00|N|06|25|00|W|type:landmark_scale:3000_region:IE}} | capacity = 4,500 (3,100 seated) | owner = Dundalk Town FC Ltd (consortium) | chrtitle = Chairperson | chairman = Chris Clinton | manager = [[Ciarán Kilduff]] | mgrtitle = Manager | league = [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] | season = [[2025 League of Ireland First Division|2025]] | position = [[League of Ireland First Division]], 1st of 10 (Champions and promoted) | website = {{URL|https://dundalkfc.com}} | pattern_b1 = _macroncerberuseco25wb | pattern_la1 = _macroncerberuseco25wb | pattern_ra1 = _macroncerberuseco25wb | pattern_sh1 = | pattern_so1 = | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = ffffff | pattern_b2 = _macronthemiseco23bw | pattern_la2 = _macronthemiseco23bw | pattern_ra2 = _macronthemiseco23bw | pattern_sh2 = | shorts2 = 000000 | socks2 = 000000 | current = 2026 Dundalk F.C. season }} '''Dundalk Football Club''' ({{IPAc-en|d|ʌ|n|ˈ|d|ɔː|(|l|)|k}} {{respell|dun|DAW(L)K}}) is a professional [[association football|football]] club that competes in the [[League of Ireland Premier Division]], the top tier of [[Association football in the Republic of Ireland|football in the Republic of Ireland]]. It was founded in 1903 as Dundalk G.N.R., the [[Works team#Europe|works-team]] of the [[Great Northern Railway (Ireland)|Great Northern Railway]]. It is based in [[Dundalk]], [[County Louth]] and its home ground is [[Oriel Park]]. The club crest is three [[martlet]]s on a shield, which was adopted from the town's [[Dundalk#Coat of arms|coat of arms]]. The team's traditional kit colours are white shirts (giving the team their nickname 'the Lilywhites') with black shorts and white or black socks. The Dundalk women's team competes in the Women's Development League (WDL), the second tier of women's football in Ireland. Dundalk were a junior club until they were invited to join the [[Leinster Senior League (association football)|Leinster Senior League]] in 1922–23. After four seasons at that level, they were elected to the [[League of Ireland]] for the [[1926–27 Dundalk F.C. season|1926–27]] season. [[1932–33 Dundalk F.C. season|Six seasons later]], they became the first club from outside [[Dublin]] to win the league title. They are the only club to have won a league title or an FAI Cup in every decade since the 1930s, with four distinct eras of success: the mid-1960s, the late-1970s/early-1980s under [[Jim McLaughlin (footballer)|Jim McLaughlin]], the late-1980s/early-1990s under [[Turlough O'Connor (footballer)|Turlough O'Connor]], and the 2010s led by [[Stephen Kenny (football manager)|Stephen Kenny]]. They have won 48 trophies at national level as of 2025, including 14 League titles and 12 [[FAI Cup]]s (with four League and Cup '[[Double (association football)|Doubles]]'), and have won a further 21 trophies at All-Ireland and provincial level.{{efn|see [[Dundalk F.C.#Honours|Honours]]}} They were also the winners of both the [[Dublin and Belfast Inter-City Cup|first]] and the [[Champions Cup (All-Ireland)|most recent]] All-Ireland club competitions. They made their [[Dundalk F.C. in European football|European]] debut in the [[1963–64 European Cup]], and that season became the first Irish side to win an away match in Europe. Their best performance in the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] was in [[1979–80 European Cup|1979–80]], when they reached the last 16, and they reached the last 16 of the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|European Cup Winners' Cup]] in [[1981–82 European Cup Winners' Cup|1981–82]]. They are the only Irish club to have qualified more than once for the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] group stage and, in [[2016–17 Europa League|2016–17]], they became the first team from Ireland to both win points and win a match at that level of European competition. They remain the only Irish team to have won points in the Europa League group stage as of the 2026–27 European season."}}
